p: The Confederate tendency to overshoot was a significant tactical failure — the cannonade inflicted far less damage on the Union infantry than Lee and Alexander had hoped.

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (chronology commentary)
p.short: Site chronology commentary on “Confederate artillery fire overshooting Cemetery Ridge — most shells landing behind the…”, Day 3

p: Alexander's first message to Pickett: 'For God's sake come quick or we cannot support you — ammunition nearly exhausted.' Pickett shows it to Longstreet. Longstreet cannot speak — nods his head. The charge is set in motion.

p.short: Site chronology entry “Alexander's first message to Pickett: 'For God's sake come quick or we cannot support you —…”, Day 3

p: Longstreet later wrote: 'I could not speak. I bowed in answer.' His reluctance to order the charge is evident in every account.

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (chronology commentary)
p.short: Site chronology commentary on “Alexander's first message to Pickett: 'For God's sake come quick or we cannot support you —…”, Day 3

p: Alexander's second message to Pickett: 'I would not make the charge now — but the order has been given and the troops are already moving.' Pickett's division steps out of the woods.

p.short: Site chronology entry “Alexander's second message to Pickett: 'I would not make the charge now — but the order has…”, Day 3

p: Union artillery falls silent — Confederate infantry interpret this as success of the cannonade. In fact Hunt has ordered silence to conserve ammunition. Confederate infantry begin dressing their lines in the open.

p.short: Site chronology entry “Union artillery falls silent — Confederate infantry interpret this as success of the cannonade.”, Day 3

p: Stannard's Vermont Brigade (I Corps) takes position south of The Angle on Cemetery Ridge. Stannard has a clear view of Kemper's right flank. He is already planning the flanking maneuver.

p.short: Site chronology entry “Stannard's Vermont Brigade (I Corps) takes position south of The Angle on Cemetery Ridge.”, Day 3

p: PICKETT'S CHARGE BEGINS. The entire Confederate assault force — approximately 12,500 men in a mile-wide front — steps off Seminary Ridge in Line of Battle heading east across the open fields toward Cemetery Ridge. The most famous infantry assault in American history.

p.short: Site chronology entry “Pickett's Charge Begins”, Day 3

p: Union artillery opens with solid shot then shell as the Confederate line advances across the open ground. Each discharge tears gaps in the Confederate line. The attackers close ranks and keep moving.

p.short: Site chronology entry “Union artillery opens with solid shot then shell as the Confederate line advances across the…”, Day 3

p: BROCKENBROUGH COLLAPSES. The far Confederate left (Brockenbrough's Virginia brigade) breaks and retreats under flanking fire from the 8th Ohio's advanced skirmish position. Pettigrew's left flank is now exposed.

Confederate assault line reaches the Emmitsburg Road and crosses the fencing. Heavy casualties from Union artillery and musketry. Kemper's brigade begins obliquing left toward the Copse of Trees — exposing its right flank.

p.short: Site chronology entry “Confederate assault line reaches the Emmitsburg Road and crosses the fencing.”, Day 3

p: STANNARD'S FLANKING ATTACK. Stannard's Vermont brigade wheels left 90 degrees and pours enfilade fire into Kemper's exposed right flank. The 13th and 14th Vermont fire into the Confederate right. Kemper's brigade takes devastating flank fire.

p.short: Site chronology entry “Stannard's Flanking Attack”, Day 3

p: Kemper severely wounded in the Confederate assault. Mayo assumes brigade command. Kemper briefly captured, then rescued by his men.

p.short: Site chronology entry “Kemper severely wounded in the Confederate assault.”, Day 3

p: Pettigrew's Confederate brigades (26th NC, 11th NC, 47th NC, 52nd NC) reach the stone wall on Cemetery Ridge north of The Angle. Union II Corps (Smyth, Hays) fires at close range. 12th NJ fires buck-and-ball at point-blank range.

p.short: Site chronology entry “Pettigrew's Confederate brigades (26th NC, 11th NC, 47th NC, 52nd NC) reach the stone wall…”, Day 3

p: Garnett's Confederate brigade reaches the stone wall at The Angle. Heavy casualties from canister. Garnett rides on horseback (too ill to walk) — conspicuous and exposed. The two lines exchange fire at close range across the wall.

p.short: Site chronology entry “Garnett's Confederate brigade reaches the stone wall at The Angle.”, Day 3

p: GARNETT KIA. Shot from his horse at The Angle — his body never officially identified after the battle. Marshall killed leading Pettigrew's brigade. Multiple Confederate commanders fall almost simultaneously.

ARMISTEAD LEADS MEN OVER THE WALL. Armistead places his hat on his sword as a guide and leads his brigade over the stone wall at The Angle — the deepest Confederate penetration of the battle. Approximately 150-200 men cross with him.

p.short: Site chronology entry “Armistead Leads Men Over The Wall”, Day 3
